title: Dispute handling lacks time bounds, independence controls, idempotency and participant status notification

original_titles.title: GET /receipts/{id} missing; POST dispute not idempotent; GET own disputes missing
Disqualify/reinstate/merge with two-person approval missing (PT-04a S2)
Dispute submission lacks idempotency key, deadline countdown and status tracking (P-16)

problem: Dispute routes and organizer resolution exist, but participant dispute creation/idempotency/deadline/status UX is incomplete, and resolution can be handled by an organizer without an independence/two-person check. Reviewers cannot access the intended dispute surface.
impact: Duplicate disputes, late disputes, conflicted resolutions or missing feedback can make score appeals difficult to trust.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define dispute window and eligible grounds in the published competition rules. Enforce the deadline server-side using DB time.
Add an Idempotency-Key to dispute creation and participant GET own disputes/status routes with cursor pagination.
Separate dispute investigator/resolver permissions from the original reviewer and require a second approver for material point changes.
Record a mandatory resolution reason, evidence links, adjustment ledger entry and notification/outbox event in one transaction.
Test duplicate create, late create, conflicted reviewer, two-approver correction and result visibility after resolution.

acceptance_criteria: A participant can file only within the published window and receives a durable receipt.
Resolution is independently authorized, reasoned and auditable.
Every status transition is visible to the participant.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
